known_divergences.reason: Prints the directory of the running binary, so the two tools differ by installation path alone.
jq 1.7.1 aborts (`Assertion failed: JVP_HAS_KIND(j, JV_KIND_STRING)`, jv.c:1370) on a non-string format; succinctly reports a catchable error.
Same jq 1.7.1 assertion abort on a non-string format as strftime/1.
On `"a" | strptime(.)` the weekday of 1900-00-00 is 6 in jq 1.7.1 on macOS, `[…,8,367]` on glibc, and `[…,0,-1]` in succinctly; the value is platform-libc dependent (#5340).
add(f) is new in jq 1.8; succinctly follows the 1.7.1 pin (ADR-0018).
trimstr(s) is new in jq 1.8; succinctly follows the 1.7.1 pin (ADR-0018).
have_decnum is new in jq 1.8; succinctly follows the 1.7.1 pin (ADR-0018).
have_literal_numbers is new in jq 1.8; succinctly follows the 1.7.1 pin (ADR-0018).
`--version` names the tool (`succinctly jq ... 0.8.0`), not jq's version token.
`-h` prints succinctly's own usage text.
`--help` prints succinctly's own usage text.
`--build-configuration` describes succinctly's build, not jq's configure line.
succinctly has no bytecode to disassemble; the flag is rejected (exit 2).
succinctly has no bytecode to trace; the flag is rejected (exit 2).
jq reads the remaining files after one cannot be opened (and exits 2); succinctly stops at the first missing file.

`tojson` of a value built 1000 levels deep: jq answers; succinctly raises `nesting depth exceeds limit of 384` (exit 5) for a value it built itself. The ceiling stays since #5497, which aligned parsing and printing with jq: lifting it is a design of its own (ADR-0025), recorded in the Nesting depth section of docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md.

Same as deep-tojson-built-1000, at 10000 levels. The ceiling stays since #5497, which aligned parsing and printing with jq: lifting it is a design of its own (ADR-0025), recorded in the Nesting depth section of docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md.

Same as deep-tojson-built-1000, at 20000 levels. The ceiling stays since #5497, which aligned parsing and printing with jq: lifting it is a design of its own (ADR-0025), recorded in the Nesting depth section of docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md.

`==` on a value built 5000 levels deep: jq answers; succinctly raises the 384-level depth error. The ceiling stays since #5497, which aligned parsing and printing with jq: lifting it is a design of its own (ADR-0025), recorded in the Nesting depth section of docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md.

`sort` over a value built 3000 levels deep: jq answers; succinctly raises the 384-level depth error. The ceiling stays since #5497, which aligned parsing and printing with jq: lifting it is a design of its own (ADR-0025), recorded in the Nesting depth section of docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md.

`error(<value built 2000 levels deep>)` caught and measured: jq answers; succinctly raises the 384-level depth error. The ceiling stays since #5497, which aligned parsing and printing with jq: lifting it is a design of its own (ADR-0025), recorded in the Nesting depth section of docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md.
A user-defined function recursing 10000 deep: jq answers (about 3 s); succinctly's stack guard refuses with `exceeded maximum recursion depth` (ADR-0025).
Recursion 100000 deep: jq does not finish within 10 s; succinctly's stack guard refuses (ADR-0025).
Tail-position recursion 100000 deep: jq does not finish within 10 s; succinctly's stack guard refuses (ADR-0025), so it gets no tail-call elimination.

`[match("a";"g")]` over 100000 characters: jq 1.7.1 does not finish within 10 s on an M4 Pro (5.7 s on a 7950X); succinctly answers in tens of milliseconds. Whether jq beats the deadline depends on the host.
`gsub("a";"b")` over 100000 characters: jq 1.7.1 does not finish within 10 s; succinctly answers in tens of milliseconds.
`[] | .[1e12] = 1`: jq aborts (SIGSEGV); succinctly refuses the index with an error (exit 5, #5500).
